text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Draft law envisages 140 million kuna increase for social care funds than in the past year.
- Tangerine groves from Neretva valley in Croatia's south-eastern corner this winter had a record crop of 20,000 tonnes of fruit. Farmers are pleased with stable prices.
- Croatian managers in a recent poll by the business weekly Privredni Vjesnik show "restrained optimism" in their expectations for next year.
- Jadranski Naftovod, which operates the Adriatic pipeline, may become a new blue chip on the stock market, says minister of economy Davor Stern.
- Bankruptcy law to come into force next year, will benefit the economy by preventing trade to delay payements to producers, minister of economy Davor Stern says.
- 1,000 teachers and social workers protested in Zagreb on Tuesday demanding a 15 percent pay rise from January which would be 10 percent more than the government's offer.
- Able managers should get a change to buy remaining state-owned companies at a cheaper price, says Miljenko Weiss, vice-president of the state privatisation agency.
- American financial consultant Thomas Apperson says small entrepreneurs cannot pay high interest charged in Croatia for loans to start their business.
- Securities commission, set up in October, still unable to enforce adequate market supervision.
- IMF might extend Croatia a $400-500 million loan between years 1997 and 1999 provided its board approves a three-year economic programme proposed by the government.
- Croatia will not yield under international pressures trying to push it into the Balkans or to Europe's south-eastern region, says National Security Council.
- The rise of unemployment halted in November, when total jobless fell to 266,644 or 0.4 percent from October.

- Recently opened Zagreb unit of Italy's Cassa di Risparmio di Trieste to start credit operations for its clients among citizens next year, says director Adriano Carisi. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 3835-1-4557075
